title: Making room for spiritual experience
summary: A starting point for understanding the person’s experience, meaning and preferences before applying a label.
text: making room for spiritual experience a starting point for understanding the person’s experience, meaning and preferences before applying a label. start with the person’s language faith, belonging, conscience or the meaning of life may arise in a conversation. none automatically establishes a spiritual need. our proposed starting point is to ask what the person means in their own words. requiring the label “spirituality” and imposing that label are two different ways of narrowing the conversation. discussion is not consent to a practice sharing a topic is not the same as requesting a religious practice or the practitioner’s interpretation. someone may want to describe prayer without wanting to pray together during a session. this educational note proposes discussing the topic’s importance, the wish to address it, and consent to a particular method separately. resources, struggles and goals as you read, consider three separate notes: what this experience means, what supports or troubles the person, and what help they want. nonbelief should not be treated as a deficit. not discussing spirituality is also a valid preference. these are proposed areas of inquiry, not a scale or fixed intervention sequence.

title: Reading a finding together with its limits
summary: A short reading structure that separates research, interpretation and recommendation.
text: reading a finding together with its limits a short reading structure that separates research, interpretation and recommendation. the studies may ask different questions one study may examine client preferences, another religious similarity and another adapted treatment outcomes. rather than treating them as repetitions of one finding, write down each actual question. this site displays source type separately from the title. the existence of guidance does not mean an intervention effect has been measured. keep the comparator visible in captari and colleagues’ meta-analysis, the more rigorous additive comparisons found no significant advantage for psychological distress, but better spiritual well-being. keep these outcomes separate. a nonsignificant difference does not prove equivalence. the record also does not automatically establish the effect of a specific theory-based spiritual integration. write your inference separately test a reading note with three sentences: what the source directly shows, what it does not show, and what new question it raises. the last sentence may be your interpretation or recommendation; do not report it as a finding. reporting checklists support transparency but cannot themselves repair a design problem.

title: Preference, competence and professional boundaries
summary: Keeping the relationship between the client’s wishes and the practitioner’s capabilities explicit.
text: preference, competence and professional boundaries keeping the relationship between the client’s wishes and the practitioner’s capabilities explicit. similarity is not competence start from the assumption that a shared worldview does not guarantee understanding. the proposed self-check is whether we hear the actual request or mistake personal comfort for competence. disagreement alone does not establish that working together is impossible. specific knowledge, skills and limits require separate consideration. being able to disagree collaboration should not mean agreeing with every interpretation. a proposed conversational stance is: “am i understanding you correctly; what needs changing?” that sentence alone does not remove unequal power. how refusal is received and whose request shapes the goal matter too. making limits visible explain the rationale, intended function and alternatives of a proposed practice. consider appropriate supervision and support at competence limits. educational content here does not make individualized decisions. a crisis or immediate risk should not be managed through a web reading; use local emergency and professional support channels.

title: Not treating culture as a ready-made explanation
summary: Considering belonging, support, commitment and constrained options without reducing one to another.
text: not treating culture as a ready-made explanation considering belonging, support, commitment and constrained options without reducing one to another. from label to experience religious or cultural affiliation alone does not tell us what someone wants in counseling. this dossier proposes following a question about affiliation with inquiry into its lived meaning. the same community may be experienced as supportive and difficult. keeping both possibilities open challenges a single, uniform notion of culture. noticing metaphysical assumptions hodge offers a theoretical discussion of metaphysical assumptions in mental health discourse. one reading question is whether practitioners treat their own position as the sole standard of neutrality. this is not a claim that all metaphysical views are clinically identical or that one is more effective. commitment and available options a commitment can be meaningful while surrounded by difficult conditions. we propose distinguishing what the person wants to preserve, available options and the cost of acting differently. staying or leaving is not predetermined as success. respect for culture should not make concrete harm or safety needs invisible.

title: Before choosing an instrument
summary: Four separate checks for construct, intended use, translation and rights.
text: before choosing an instrument four separate checks for construct, intended use, translation and rights. look beyond the name spiritual well-being, spiritual struggle, religious commitment and preference for integration are not the same measurement. start by naming the construct in your question. then inspect what the instrument measures, in which population and for what purpose. popularity is not evidence that a tool fits your question. translation, adaptation and permission a translated form does not establish evidence for its intended use. permission and validity evidence are different matters. fica’s official page requires written permission for excerpts, translation and adaptation. marsam therefore links to the original rather than republishing items or presenting its own translation as an instrument. create an instrument record keep original source, version, target population, response format, permissions and adaptation study in separate fields. when information is missing, record the gap rather than guessing. this catalog is a starting point for selection. it does not produce diagnoses, automated scores or clinical decisions.

title: From a question to a research design
summary: A working note that makes claim type, data structure and authorization visible from the start.
text: from a question to a research design a working note that makes claim type, data structure and authorization visible from the start. write the question in one sentence this dossier does not select a method for you. start by stating whose experience you will examine and in which context. describing prevalence, examining an association and testing an intervention are different questions. when the question changes, reconsider the data required and the permissible inference. make the data structure explicit repeated observations from one person, linked observations from two people and independent samples are not the same analysis unit. check that session counts do not replace independent participant counts. instead of a universal sample size, justify the target question, model and plausible missing-data conditions. before collecting data the proposed marsam research record includes the responsible researcher, required ethics and institutional approvals, consent, data responsibility, storage and withdrawal procedures. none is presented as already secured. this preview collects no participant responses. open science does not mean openly publishing identifiable or unauthorized data.

title: Reading theory alongside spiritual experience
summary: Compare views of the person, change and boundaries rather than assembling a common technique list.
text: reading theory alongside spiritual experience compare views of the person, change and boundaries rather than assembling a common technique list. identify the theory’s question when reading an approach, note how it explains difficulty and where it locates change. then ask how spiritual experience enters that account. spiritual vocabulary alone does not establish theoretical integration. avoid treating distinct approaches as different names for the same techniques. compare the same dimensions the proposed theory records use five fields: view of the person, explanation of difficulty, change goals, relation to spiritual experience and scope of evidence. this is not an efficacy ranking. the volume edited by eksi is a reading resource connecting theories and spiritual dimensions; only its publisher record is provided here. record tensions as well an integration note should not end with similarities. which assumptions about autonomy, commitment, reality or change differ? this is a proposed reading question. theoretical compatibility alone does not establish suitability for a particular person or clinical superiority. practice decisions require separate competence and assessment.

title: Keeping human responsibility in digital tools
summary: Proposed boundaries for AI-assisted content, translation and research tools.
text: keeping human responsibility in digital tools proposed boundaries for ai-assisted content, translation and research tools. fluent text is not verified knowledge the proposed marsam workflow does not label ai output as scientific publication. source identity, support for a claim and editorial decisions remain separate. a real title or doi does not validate every interpretation. a professional interface does not increase the evidential strength of its content. preserve meaning in translation “associated with” must not become “causes” in translation. population, context, uncertainty and source limitations should survive across languages. content exists in eight languages in this preview, but native-language expert and scientific editor approval have not been given. each reading page makes that status visible. before entering data into a system this prototype does not collect clinical notes, survey responses or identity data. its contribution tool creates a local file only and asks users not to enter private data. any future tool needs a separately designed purpose, responsibility, access, retention and deletion framework. technical correctness is not clinical benefit or ethics approval.
